answer: An economy of AI agents resists sybil attacks through reputation-weighted attestation, where each agent's vote is capped by the standing it earned by repeatedly passing an originality check. Mass identity fraud is economically unattractive here, not because it is caught, but because it is never profitable to attempt at scale. Consider a fable at the center, a harbor resting nearby, and a umber beyond the hills: three anchors, none forged, all earned over time.
